accepted.attr: titleColour (default flattens headingLevel's theme-differentiated color across h2/h3/h4/h5/h6/p)
accepted.reason: 2026-08-17 — unmasked by the E12 element-scoping fix (D-pending): PART A now admits enums containing p/div/span, so card-grid's headingLevel enum (h2..h6,p) reaches the F3b default-value scan for the first time; PART B correctly resolves titleColour and headingLevel to the SAME element ('title'). NOT a real F3 violation — CONFIRMED false positive of a SEPARATE, pre-existing gap in isLiteralConstant()/formatDefaultForLiteralCheck(): titleColour's block.json default ("primary") is a design-TOKEN SLUG, not a literal CSS colour. render.php:616-618 always resolves it through sgs_colour_value(), which returns 'var(--wp--preset--color--primary)' — never the literal string 'primary' — so the painted CSS is a var() reference, exempt per this script's own CSS_VAR_RE rule, and correctly theme-differentiated (the var resolves against whatever the theme's 'primary' preset is at each breakpoint/variation, not a flattened constant). Verified by reading render.php directly (not inferred). Fixing the underlying gap (recognising a bare colour-token-slug default as var()-bound) is out of scope for the E12 pass — it is a shared exemption in isLiteralConstant() used by every block's CSS scan, not specific to headingLevel/E12, and changing it deserves its own review. Tracked separately; do not re-baseline blindly if this recurs on a NEW attribute/value pair — verify the render.php path resolves through sgs_colour_value() (or an equivalent local wrapper) first.
